newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, France agree to set up military committee.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, France agree to set up military committee.

text.p: Qatar and France have agreed to set up a high-level military committee to boost cooperation and safeguard security in the volatile Gulf, France's defence minister said on Sunday.

"We have agreed to put in place a high-level joint committee in which the generals of the French and Qatari military will be members to strengthen cooperation in protecting and upholding the security of the region", Charles Millon told reporters.

The committee will be set up within two months. France will advise oil and gas-rich Qatar on "technical matters, such as appropriate equipment, renewal of equipment and maintenance of equipment", Millon said.
He was speaking on a visit to Qatar in which he met with senior officials.

France, Britain and the United States all have defence treaties with Qatar, whose oil and gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's -- make it a strategic source of vital clean energy in the next century.
The three Western powers are in fierce competition to sell 50 main battle tank's to Qatar's 8,000-man army.
Paris is a major weapons supplier to Doha.
Britain and Qatar last month signed a $825 million deal to supply Doha with armoured personnel carriers, patrol boats, missiles and Hawk trainer aircraft.
Millon dismissed a reporter's suggestion that France had lost out to Britain in the deal, insisting that French-Qatari relations were "permanent" and "at a very high level".
"France has a role to play in the region and is always eager to help the Gulf states to strengthen their security," he said.

Gulf Arab security fears following Iraq's lightning invasion of Kuwait in 1990 has turned the oil-rich region into a lucrative arms market where billions of dollars have been poured into weapons purchases.
France has lobbied agressively in the Gulf for its arms makers.
